items.summary: Data centers are thirstier than most people realize, but not because of the water pumped into their on-site cooling equipment.

items.title: New rules let PepsiCo integrate emissions certificates into its carbon accounts
items.summary: When the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) said in June that it would give companies more flexibility in tackling supply-chain emissions, the decision won applause from businesses that have been struggling to shrink that part of their footprint.

items.title: More UK businesses increasing investment in heat adaptation, survey finds
items.summary: According to Barclays’ latest Business Prosperity Index, 60% of businesses have either already invested or are looking to invest in extreme heat adaptation measures.

items.title: Plug-in solar hits market to help British households cut bills
items.summary: From today (27 August), the easy-to-use plug-in solar panels are legal to buy and use, potentially helping homes knock £110 of their energy bills.

items.title: There is no such thing as ‘sustainable paint’, so why does the industry keep marketing it as eco-friendly?
items.summary: As regulators tighten greenwashing rules and scrutiny of chemicals such as PFAS grows, Farrow & Ball’s head of R&D Gareth Hayfield argues that paintmakers must move beyond vague environmental claims towards transparency and evidence-based communications.

items.title: THREE WEEKS to go until edie’s Sustainable Supply Chains Summit
items.summary: Join us on 17 September for a unique opportunity to gain expert-led insights through thought leadership and industry panels featuring top professionals in sustainability, supply chain and procurement.

items.title: Two data centres set to emit more than ExxonMobil’s UK operations, analysis warns
items.summary: Two upcoming data centres will emit 4.5 million tonnes of carbon a year when fully running, analysis by non-profit Foxglove has found, exceeding fossil fuel company ExxonMobil’s entire UK emissions.
